entries.subject: Kilic et al. (2026) multi-chord occultation global limb fit
entries.finding: The selected outline is the 2020-2023 global projected ellipse with semiaxes 363.42 (+3.53/-3.85) and 333.98 (+7.07/-4.96) km; the edge-on illustration assumes an equatorial depth equal to the long projected diameter, so the 726.84 x 726.84 x 667.96 km full axes are not a measured three-dimensional shape.

entries.subject: Older thermal-size-only size illustrations
entries.finding: The README records that the 2026 combined multi-chord fit supersedes the older thermal-size-only illustrations, so they are not used for the displayed model.
entries.revisitWhen: A new thermal or radiometric analysis supersedes the 2026 combined occultation fit.

entries.subject: Rotation period and inertial pole
entries.finding: The README records that the 12.4-hour period estimate is not secure in the 2026 analysis and that no measured pole or current rotational phase is installed; the display uses an illustrative ICRF pole with an arbitrary prime meridian.
entries.revisitWhen: A secure rotation period or a measured inertial pole for Ixion is published.

entries.subject: True flattening and polar depth
entries.finding: The selected ellipse constrains only the projected limb, so the README states that true flattening and depth remain unresolved.
entries.revisitWhen: An occultation campaign or resolved imaging constrains the third axis.

entries.subject: cssEarth missing-coverage grid as the surface
entries.finding: No resolved global imagery or topographic mesh was supplied by the selected occultation study, so the manifest supplies the project-authored missing-coverage grid and the normal grid marks unmapped terrain with Shadows off by default.
